items: Stage A: purpose, owners, study boundary and plan.

Stage C: shortfalls, their consequences and next-review decision.
Stage D: work allocation, alternatives and delivery strategy.
Stage E: measurable accountability and oversight.
Stage F: implementable roles, terms and delivery documents.

This lesson explains a general method. It does not include specialist requirements for every field or organization.
Completing the exercises does not establish authority to approve work, enter agreements, or certify compliance.
The six study stages are instructional labels rather than a prescribed universal procedure.
Real project limits, operating conditions and delegated authority are not included.
The supplied reference collection is extensive. This compact study guide does not reproduce or validate each specialist rule, form, annex or procedure in it.
Inferred: Exercises, choices and arithmetic values are made up solely to practise a method.
Inferred: The workload simulation is a capped illustrative plan and separate surge case; it is not a real forecast.
The four assessment dimensions are an educational structure; each actual project must choose its relevant criteria.
Inferred: The short chapter examples are hypothetical workflows, not measured cases, procurement instructions or standards.
